items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Rodger was supposed to have his salary collected by Sid and given to him because he was the one that had found the job and formed th band... The trumpet chair had been left open for me and the band had worked in the club two weeks before I returned.

ctx.x: Things had happened quite fast and unforunately for Rodger. He had formed an orchestra with a white drummer, Jim Chapin, a Canadian pianist whose name was Bill something, a well known white bassist named Sid Wales and Jem Davis, an alto man that had a style on the order of Pete Brown. Lem and Pete both lived in Brooklyn.

The trumpet chair had been left open for me and the band had worked in the club two weeks before I returned. The club was located at 152nd East 55th Street. But Rodger Ray was not there because Sid Weiss had pulled a trick on him. Rodger's voice was not as good as he thought it was and when Sid heard him sing, and he knew that Rodger did not belong to the musicians union because he was not a musician, he reported him and a union delegate came to the club and told Rodger he could not work, because he was not a…

Sid promised Rodger that he would take charge of the orchestra until I arrived and Rodger was supposed to have his salary collected by Sid and given to him because he was the one that had found the job and formed th band.
